summary: All five acceptance criteria are present, faithful and in scope. (a) Rounds render per card, in caller-supplied array order, proved with THREE rounds twice — at component level (OrgThread.test.tsx:25-51, deliberately out-of-chronological timestamps, asserted by DOM order via compareDocumentPosition, not just presence) and on the actual page (OrgPage.thread.test.tsx:84-115, which also asserts the thread follows its LeadCard in DOM order, closing Trap 2's 'component exists but is unmounted' hole). (b) An unanswered round renders as a distinct open row ('Open — waiting for your answer', OrgThread.tsx:52-61); an empty-string answer is treated as unanswered (isAnswered, OrgThread.tsx:36-38) and is separately tested. (c) Round text reaches the DOM only as plain JSX text nodes — no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, no markdown, no parser; the fixture with markup + the sentinel produces no real /, no window.__pwned, and no notification (OrgThread.test.tsx:81-115). Consistent with FR-04.37's outgoing direction (AC FR-04.19, spec L2549). (d) Every 'no thread' shape (undefined / [] / rounds: []) renders literally nothing (OrgThread.tsx:68, :90-91; tests :117-143), and the production truth is preserved because useOrgThreads returns {} and the pre-existing OrgPage.test.tsx does NOT mock it. (e) Not executable in this review environment (no shell); statically the new tests reuse the exact `as ReturnType` mock-cast pattern and the `eslint-disable-next-line no-bitwise` directive already present in the passing OrgPage.test.tsx, so no new type/lint shape is introduced. Scope: the touched set is exactly OrgThread.tsx, OrgThread.test.tsx, useOrgThreads.ts, OrgPage.tsx (+8 lines, mount only), OrgPage.thread.test.tsx, org.css, plus the mini-plan — no inbox card, no board surface, no claim chip, no leadwright path, no poFeedback field (Trap 1), no leadwright-side producer (Trap 3). The useOrgThreads stub is the minimum seam needed to mount the display and is documented as such, not a fabricated data source. Stage 2 (code-reviewer) may proceed.
non_blocking_observations: OrgThread.test.tsx:87 stubs window.Notification, but the client uses no Web Notifications API anywhere — the codebase's only 'notification' concept is the <task-notification> envelope parsed in client/src/external/session-parser.ts:697-704. AC-c still holds substantively (the thread text never enters that parser, and the inert-text assertions carry the proof), but the notification half of that test asserts against a mechanism this app does not use.
ThreadRound.askedAt is a required field that nothing renders (answeredAt likewise). Harmless, no contract impact — a data-model field ahead of its display.
